intro: Phrase statistics depend on overlapping windows: repeated phrases should increase a count, while a short document may contain no complete window.
task: Build an overlapping phrase counter and inspect how repeated windows differ from a vocabulary set.
requirements: tokens is a list or tuple of at most 10000 nonempty strings; n is an integer from 1 to 10000. Tokens are already segmented and case is significant.
Return a dictionary whose keys are tuples of n adjacent tokens and whose values are integer occurrence counts. Count overlapping windows.
Return an empty dictionary for an empty sequence or when n exceeds the token count. Do not join tokens into ambiguous string keys.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Slide one position
hints.body: Advance the start index by one even after finding a repeated phrase.

hints.title: Keep token boundaries
hints.body: A tuple distinguishes a multiword token from two separate tokens.

explanation: There are max(0, L-n+1) windows in a sequence of length L. Counting these windows produces a multiset rather than a set of phrases.
Overlaps are essential: the bigram (a,a) occurs twice in three consecutive a tokens. This representation is useful for corpus diagnostics and language-model statistics.
